theorem_title: The 732 gadget replacement does not decrease size
natural_language_statement:
Call a subset of positive integers admissible if it contains no $a<b<c$ satisfying $a(b+c)=bc$, equivalently $1/a=1/b+1/c$. Write $G=\{122,183,244,366,732\}$ and $B=\{122,183,244\}$. For a Boolean membership predicate $S:\mathbb N\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, let $R(S)$ replace its selections in $G$ by exactly $B$ and leave every other membership decision unchanged. If $S$ is admissible and supported in $\{1,\ldots,732\}$, then

$$
|S|\leq |R(S)|.
$$

This is the quantitative half of the replacement argument. The source cardinal function counts membership on the duplicate-free domain consisting of the gadget and its complement in 1 through 732.
